text:
Emily: Quick sync — we need a consumer contract for GPU telemetry across Hosted + Dedicated pools. Focus: SM occupancy, per-GPU memory (used/free), and queue_depth (pending requests). This will feed the new console heatmap + capacity alerts.

Akash: +1. Do we have consensus on metric names and labels? I want low-cardinality tags so aggregation stays sane for Hosted.

Priya: Can we also include a derived field for `kv_cache_utilization`? Some models leak a lot of KV and that affects usable memory. If not possible, at least export per-alloc kv_bytes.

Emily: Good call. Proposal: metric names and basic labels: 
```
- gpu.sm_occupancy_percent{pool_type, pool_id, gpu_id, region}
- gpu.memory_used_bytes{pool_type, pool_id, gpu_id, region}
- gpu.memory_total_bytes{pool_type, pool_id, gpu_id, region}
- gpu.queue_depth{pool_type, pool_id, queue_type, region}
- gpu.kv_cache_bytes{pool_type, pool_id, gpu_id, region}
```
Keep pool_type in {hosted,dedicated}. For dedicated pools we may have redacted tenant ids — see privacy note below.

Marc: For SRE/alerts, we want percentiles over 1m/5m/1h windows. Also prefer histograms for queue latency, but simple gauge for queue_depth works. High-cardinality tags = danger. Can we avoid per-tenant tags on Hosted by default?

Akash: Implementation constraints: runtime can emit per-GPU gauges every 10s without too much overhead. Histograms cost more; we'd prefer to emit summary buckets only at 1m aggregation. If telemetry pipeline supports prom-histogram style we can do it.

Lina: From product side, the console needs: (1) per-pool heatmap of SM occupancy, (2) per-tenant top N consumers (hosted only), (3) an incident-style alert when effective_headroom < 10% for 5m. How do we define effective_headroom?

Priya: Effective_headroom = min(mem_headroom_percent, sm_headroom_percent) adjusted for average queue_depth per-GPU. Rough formula: 
```
mem_headroom_percent = 100 * (memory_total - memory_used) / memory_total
sm_headroom_percent = 100 - sm_occupancy_percent
effective_headroom ≈ min(mem_headroom_percent, sm_headroom_percent) - alpha * queue_depth_normalized
```
Set alpha=2 for initial tuning.

Emily: That formula works as a derived consumer metric (console and alerts). We should publish it as `gpu.effective_headroom_percent{pool_type,pool_id,region}` derived in the metrics pipeline (not emitted by runtime).

Marc: A few operational asks:
- Emit `pool_id` consistently (no nulls).
- Add `instance_id` for on-host mapping to node for SRE debug.
- Tag dedicated pools with `customer_masked_id` (hashed), never raw tenant id in hosted metrics unless customer opts in.

Akash: Runtime note: we can include `instance_id` and `pool_id`. Masking tenant ids is fine, but hosted per-tenant top-N requires a separate telemetry path with explicit consent; we can set a flag to include `tenant_id` at sampling rate 1/10 for hosted to limit cardinality.

Emily: That means two export modes: full-hosted (tenant_id enabled, sampled) and default (no tenant). Document must call out sampling rates and retention.

Priya: Sampling implications for ML: downsampled tenant_id is ok for top-N only. For cost attribution we still need accurate counters — maybe export a separate `billing.tokens_consumed{pool_id, tenant_masked}` aggregated at 5m.

Marc: Alerts: suggest these initial thresholds for Hosted default pools: 
- Warning: effective_headroom < 20% for 10m
- Critical: effective_headroom < 10% for 5m
Also add alert for sustained queue_depth per-GPU > 50 for 5m.

Lina: Console UX: heatmap color scale should be occupancy percent with hover showing memory used/total, queue_depth, last_seen. Ability to filter by region/pool_type and to drill to per-gpu view. Also a small sparkline for effective_headroom.

Akash: Telemetry schema notes: prefer snake_case metric names, units in bytes/percent, include prometheus-style `unit` label? Pipeline can coerce. We'll include unit in metric metadata.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: new metric contract PR required in repo infra/telemetry-schemas by EOD Thu. See template: https://internal.redwood/telemetry-schemas/template.md

Emily: Action items: 
- Akash: add runtime exporter changes + sampling flag PR (due Tue)
- Priya: list derived metric formulas + validation prompts for ML regressions (due Wed)
- Marc: draft alert rules and runbook (due Wed)
- Lina: mockups for heatmap + drilldown (due Thu)
- Emily: write consumer contract doc and open PR (due Thu EOD)

Akash: Quick Q — what's the retention expectation? 90d for raw per-GPU? Or 30d to save cost?

Marc: Ops preference: 30d raw at 10s resolution, and 90d rolled-up (1m/5m) aggregated. We can work with that.

Priya: For ML evals we might need 6mo of aggregated metrics at 5m. Can we add an archive path for that?

Emily: Yes — pipeline will support cold storage. Document that aggregated 5m/1h metrics kept 6mo.

Lina: Final: please make sure dedicated customers have opt-out docs and privacy text. Anyone from legal looped?

Emily: I'll loop legal after PR. If no other blockers let's get the PR started — thanks everyone :thumbsup:

telemetry-bot: PR template link posted: https://internal.redwood/telemetry-schemas/new

Marc: I'll start a draft for the alert runbook and post in #eng-sre later today.

Akash: I'll open the runtime exporter PR now and ping reviewers.

Priya: I'll validate derived metric against a 2-week load sim and report numbers.

Emily: Great — we'll reconvene Fri 10am to review PR + mockups.
